morning.label: Risk-On Tilt
morning.summary: The AI trade recharged overnight: AMD crossed a $1T valuation and Meta's Muse AI agent drove Monday's best S&P 500 day since early August, with Nasdaq at a record close. Oil breaking below $100 on the Iran-Hormuz reopening report adds a fresh tailwind into the open. The main offsets are lingering Nvidia growth fears amid the euphoria and today's event risk — Trump's UN address and the start of the Fed speaker circuit.

morning.take: The AI bid is real and broad — AMD in the $1T club, Meta's Muse bump, Bitcoin and copper screaming risk-on — and oil breaking below $100 on the Hormuz headline removes the one macro brake from Monday. The only thing that can wreck this session is event risk: Trump's UN speech and Barkin's Fed-speak can talk a strong tape down. Call: UP, with the Nvidia valuation warnings as the one thing to watch if breadth thins.

morning.label: Risk-On Tilt
morning.summary: Futures pointed to a strong open as optimism around the Trump-Xi summit and progress in US-China AI talks lifted risk appetite, while oil slipped on claims of stronger Hormuz flows and yields eased. Rare-earth miners ripped on Trump's Greenland security announcement, and Coinbase, bitcoin-treasury names, and Warner Bros/Paramount climbed on fresh deal and news flow. Offsetting the mood: Novo Nordisk plunged after its 2030 obesity goals disappointed, US diesel hit a record $6.50+/gal, and Fed officials kept the hawkish drumbeat alive. Net: a risk-on premarket tempered by energy and rates crosscurrents.

morning.take: Futures ripped overnight on Trump-Xi summit talk and a Greenland-driven rare-earth frenzy — classic pre-open euphoria. But NVO's obesity-target stumble and record diesel prices are a reminder the bid is narrow. Blended 51 is barely positive: the market wants to go up, it's just not sure it should.

evening.label: Firmly Bullish
evening.summary: Monday's session was a decisive AI-led risk-on move: the Nasdaq closed at a record high (its best day since August) as chip stocks surged — AMD crossed $1T on AI demand — and falling oil prices plus retreating Treasury yields unlocked the broader rally. The only real counterweight was a hawkish Fed voice: Musalem said more rate hikes are likely needed to quell inflation, a reminder that the rally is still running ahead of policy risk.

evening.take: Monday was the kind of session that makes you want to chase — Nasdaq record, AMD crossing $1T, META's best day in over a year. The fuel is real (falling oil, retreating yields), but this rally is running on AI euphoria while a Fed official openly campaigns for more hikes. Momentum says UP for Tuesday; the risk is that good news is getting priced in very fast.

evening.label: Risk-Off Tilt
evening.summary: Across ~175 headlines, roughly two-thirds were noise — duplicates, intraday wraps, explainers restating known conditions, and opinion pieces. The genuinely new, market-moving items were few: Buffett stepping down as Berkshire chairman, hawkish remarks from Fed Chair Warsh, fresh corporate stress (VW's outlook cut, Kremlin seizing Nestlé's Russia ops, a Turkish fund scandal), and at the single-stock level, Netflix -4.8% on a Wells Fargo target cut, Boeing plunging on a CEO warning, a Wendy's franchisee bankruptcy, and a Goldman warning on S&P 500 earnings. Offsetting pockets of strength: crypto proxies surging on the week and an Accenture–Anthropic enterprise AI deal (+5.5% after hours).

evening.take: Friday's tape was a textbook 'quiet day, bad backdrop' setup: the index barely budged, but the marginal headline was almost uniformly bearish — Buffett's exit, a hawkish Fed chair, VW's warning, a Kremlin asset grab. Forecasting DOWN into Monday felt like the only honest read. The lesson, as always: weekend news flow can flip the board, and it did — SPY ripped +1.55%.
